Agrarianism
uh-GRAIR-ee-uh-niz-um
noun / doctrine
From Latin ager, “field, land,” naming the dignity of tilling and keeping the ground under the dominion God gave to man.

📖 Biblical Definition

Agrarianism, biblically understood, is the honouring of the dignity of working the ground — the tilling and keeping of the earth under the dominion and stewardship God gave to man at creation. The LORD God “took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it” (Gen 2:15), so that honest labour upon the land was man’s calling before ever sin entered. The land itself was given a holy rhythm under God’s law: six years the field was sown and the vineyard pruned, but the seventh year was “a sabbath of rest unto the land, a sabbath for the LORD” (Lev 25:3–5), that the ground might rest and the poor and the beast might eat. The Psalmist sings of the LORD who “causeth the grass to grow for the cattle, and herb for the service of man: that he may bring forth food out of the earth” (Psa 104:14), teaching that every harvest is a gift of God’s providence and not the bare product of human toil. And the Preacher observes that “the profit of the earth is for all: the king himself is served by the field” (Ecc 5:9), so that the labour of the husbandman undergirds the whole commonwealth. Thus Scripture dignifies the plough and the vineyard, commends honest labour and contentment with God’s provision, and binds the keeping of the land to the worship and rest of the LORD.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The honouring of honest labour upon the land, the keeping of the ground under God-given dominion, and the sabbath rest of the field as His providence.

AGRARIANISM, the honouring of honest labour and stewardship upon the land.

God put man in the garden to dress it and to keep it (Gen 2:15).

The land was given a sabbath rest in the seventh year (Lev 25:3–5).

The LORD brings forth food out of the earth by His providence (Psa 104:14).

The profit of the earth is for all; the king is served by the field (Ecc 5:9).

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 2:15 — "And the LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it."

Lev 25:3 — "Six years thou shalt sow thy field, and six years thou shalt prune thy vineyard, and gather in the fruit thereof;"

Psa 104:14 — "He causeth the grass to grow for the cattle, and herb for the service of man: that he may bring forth food out of the earth;"

Ecc 5:9 — "Moreover the profit of the earth is for all: the king himself is served by the field."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A creational good, not a contested doctrine; it commends stewardship of the land — but pantheist earth-worship that adores the creation rather than the Creator must be gently refused.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the creational dignity of labour upon the land. God put man in the garden to dress it and to keep it before the fall, and after the fall He bound the keeping of the land to the rhythm of sabbath rest. The husbandman’s toil is honourable; the harvest is God’s providence, not man’s achievement; and the profit of the earth is a gift for all. Against the contempt for honest manual labour, and against the modern divorce of men from the soil and the seasons, Scripture commends contentment, stewardship, and gratitude for daily bread out of the ground.

Yet a gentle warning belongs here, lest a right love of the land slide into a wrong worship of it. The modern age is prone to a pantheist earth-religion that adores creation itself — “mother earth,” the cult of nature, a green spirituality that makes the soil sacred in itself. Scripture forbids this plainly, naming those who “worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever” (Rom 1:25). The land is to be kept and stewarded, not deified. The Christian husbandman tills the ground as God’s gift and gives thanks to the Giver; he never bows to the gift in the place of the Lord who made it.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From Latin ager, “field,” the keeping of the ground under God-given dominion.

Agrarianism — from Latin ager, “field, land.”

Man was set to dress and keep the garden (Gen 2:15).

The land was given a sabbath rest under the law (Lev 25:4).

The harvest is God’s providence, not man’s bare achievement.

The profit of the earth is a gift for all (Ecc 5:9).

Usage

"Honour honest labour upon the land as a creational calling, given before ever sin entered."

"Receive the harvest as God’s providence and give thanks to the Giver, not to the gift."

"Keep and steward the land, but never worship the creature more than the Creator (Rom 1:25)."
